key_insight: Off-attractor supervision (OAS) retrains neural turbulence surrogates on states where they begin to fail, so the model learns the true Navier-Stokes response and stays physically plausible for much longer.
engineering_relevance: This makes CFD surrogates more reliable for long-rollout deployment, improving robustness, statistics, and stability beyond the training trajectory.
method: Select a few hundred off-attractor states for relabeling
Generate these states from surrogate rollouts, adversarial attacks, and dynamic perturbations
Compute DNS futures offline once per selected state and supervise the surrogate on those targets
evidence_signal: On 128^3 turbulence, OAS raised the median time to failure from 21 to 721 steps, outperforming baselines whose medians were at most 110 steps and also improving step-15 error and long-horizon statistics.
watch_item: The approach still depends on offline DNS relabeling and careful choice of attack/selection strategies, so its cost and coverage may limit scalability to larger systems.
paper_title: Staying on the Attractor: Supervising Neural Surrogates of 3D Turbulence Where They Leave It
